title: Design: Closed no-charge work order offers no Convert or Change category
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin (a user with every setting, See Financial Data included).
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide at 100% zoom.
  • Have Internal Work Orders turned on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a regular customer (not flagged), with one asset.
  • Have a closed no-charge work order of the regular customer, made for this test.
  • Open the attached picture iwo-flow2-13-06-closed-read-only.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open the closed work order.
  2. Click the three-dots menu in the header.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The header shows the No Charge badge and the line "Closed on [posting date]. To change it, reopen it from the Finance tab."

Step 2:

  • The menu has no Convert to Billable and no Change category.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R9: “From Close or invoice on, the classification and the category are locked: a closed no-charge work order shows the No Charge badge with no Convert or Change category action, on a closed internal or no-charge work order the Change Customer button on the customer card is disabled with the tooltip "Reopen the work order to change the customer." (the lock an invoiced or paid billable work order has today, S2-R7), and the header card carries the line "Closed on [posting date]. To change it, reopen it from the Finance tab."”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
